answers.answer:
Stable release: SCOPe 2.08 is the current stable release (the stable 2.08 classification was frozen in 2021 and described in Chandonia et al., NAR 2022). Latest periodic update: SCOPe 2.08 periodic updates are named with the pattern 2.08-YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2.08-2023-01-06 and later updates); under this pretrained-only condition I cannot query the current-release endpoint, so the exact date string of the most recent periodic update is unverified and should be read directly from the endpoint before citing.

Which identifier to cite: for a reproducible analysis, cite the exact full version string actually used. If you used only the frozen stable data, cite 'SCOPe 2.08' (stable). If you used any entries added after the freeze, cite the full date-stamped periodic identifier (e.g. 'SCOPe 2.08-2025-MM-DD'), because 'SCOPe 2.08' alone does not specify which periodic snapshot was used. All stable and periodic snapshots are archived with their own downloadable parseable files (dir.cla, dir.des, dir.hie, dir.com), so the dated identifier is sufficient to re-obtain the identical data set.

What the periodic label means: a periodic update is an incremental, date-stamped layer on top of the stable release. It adds newly released PDB entries that are classified automatically (by sequence/structure similarity to already-classified domains, ASTEROIDS-style) into existing families, superfamilies, folds, and classes. It does not change the stable release: existing sids, sunids, sccs strings, and the manually curated hierarchy (new folds, superfamilies, or families, and reclassifications) are only introduced in a new stable release, not in a periodic update. Consequently, periodic entries carry weaker evolutionary evidence than manually curated stable entries; automated placement in a family implies clear homology by sequence, placement at superfamily level is a homology inference, and fold/class placement implies only shared topology or secondary-structure content, not common ancestry. Limits: periodic additions should not be used as curated 'gold' annotations, and the latest periodic snapshot can be superseded, so the full date string (not just 2.08) must be recorded for reproducibility.
